$comment: Example bulk triage rules for a Jetson (L4T, Ubuntu 24.04) product. Not applied automatically: copy to <project>/CRA/Config/vex-rules.json, replace the top-level author (the default for every rule) with the project lead's name, and adjust each rule's date and reason. A rule may set its own author. The evidence rules K1, K2 and U1 set not_affected from product artifacts only; they apply only with a named author, so they do nothing until the author is filled in; then replace sha256:<image digest> in images with the digests of the images the rules were reviewed for (a named author with the placeholder left in is a format error), or write ["*"] deliberately for every image of the project. See tools/cra/README.md.
author: 專案負責人

rules.description: Kernel: the fix's code is not built into the product kernel
rules.reason: The kernel configuration check compares the fix's program files from the Linux kernel CNA record with the product kernel .config and Makefiles; when none of them is built, the vulnerable code is not in the product.

rules.description: Kernel: the fix only changes modules that are removed from the image or blocked from loading
rules.reason: The module map (scan/kernel-module-map.json) and the image's module list and modprobe configuration (CRA/Config/kernel-modules.json) show that the code cannot run on the product.

rules.description: Ubuntu package: Ubuntu marks this version not affected
rules.reason: The Ubuntu Security team's CVE Tracker marks the source package as not-affected in this release, and the installed source version has the same epoch and upstream version as the version in its note.

rules.description: Kernel: fixed by Ubuntu in a later linux-nvidia-tegra
rules.reason: Ubuntu has published a fixed kernel package; the fix reaches the product only with a newer L4T kernel, so the rows stay affected until we move to it.

set.recommendation: Plan: move to an L4T release based on linux-nvidia-tegra {kernel_fix_all} or later.

rules.description: Kernel: no fix yet, affected code is built
rules.reason: No fixed kernel package exists yet and the kernel configuration check found the affected code built, so the product is affected. No response value is set: can_not_fix would read as if the supplier cannot fix it; the real meaning is that the upstream has no fix yet and the issue is tracked.

set.detail_template: No fix is available yet from the upstream kernel for {component} (installed {installed_version}); the kernel configuration check found the affected code built into this kernel. The issue is tracked and the fix will be included in a later release when it becomes available.
set.recommendation: Track the fix in linux-nvidia-tegra and ship it in the first L4T release that contains it.

rules.description: Ubuntu package: newer fixed package available
rules.reason: Ubuntu publishes a fixed package; updating it in the next image removes the vulnerability.

set.recommendation: apt upgrade {component} to {fix_version} or later in the next image.

rules.reason: A fixed release of the Python package exists; the next release ships it.

set.recommendation: Upgrade {component} to {fix_version} or later in the next release.

rules.description: Kernel: no fix yet, configuration check undecided
rules.reason: No fixed kernel package exists and the kernel configuration check could not tell whether the affected code is built; these rows are under investigation, not assessed. They still count as not assessed in the release gate until someone checks each one.

set.detail_template: No fixed {component} version is available yet (installed {installed_version}) and the kernel configuration check could not decide whether the affected code is built.
